title: London session of the USD bond market recommended closed all day for New Year's Day — the turn-of-year corridor's synchronizing day, not one of its desyncs
source: NEWS: sifma.org/resources/guides-playbooks/holiday-schedule, RE-FETCHED direct 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 299,272 bytes — the same byte count the proposing lane reported) and parsed TWICE by two independent paths, with region attribution fixed to the page's own 'U.S. / U.K. / Japan Holiday Recommendations' headings rather than to card order. (1) Rendered DOM: the U.K. panel's 2026 tab carries 18 cards and its LAST card reads exactly ['New Year's Day 2026/2027', 'Friday, January 1, 2027'] with an EMPTY note element — the full-closure shape, structurally distinct from the 'Early Close (...)' notes carried by 12 U.S.-panel and 5 Japan-panel cards. (2) Embedded Next.js flight payload, where the 2027 tab lives behind a year toggle a rendered-DOM parse never reaches: the U.K. 2027 panel carries 18 cards and its FIRST card is the same New Year's Day 2026/2027 / Friday, January 1, 2027 / empty-note triple. The date is independently statutory on a government primary: gov.uk/bank-holidays.json (HTTP 200, 22,207 bytes), fetched direct the same day, lists '2027-01-01 | New Year's Day' in ALL THREE divisions — england-and-wales, scotland and northern-ireland — one of only six 2027 dates statutory across all three. Filed estimate on the same three counts as every sifma-* entry already on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an industry trade association's recommended schedule, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and SIFMA's own page states its schedule is a recommendation ('On behalf of financial markets participants, SIFMA recommends a holiday schedule for financial markets in the U.S., U.K. and Japan') rather than a market-wide halt each firm is bound by. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research (docs/research/events/sifma-uk-bond-market-closure-2027-01-01.md), which read the one prior proposal first per EVENT-RESEARCH.md — proposals/sifma-uk-bond-market-closure-2027-01-01.from-new-years-day-market-closure-2027-01-01.json, filed 2026-09-09 — and then re-fetched and re-parsed every primary rather than inheriting any of them. The proposal's date, sources and reasoning all reproduced; it is now shadowed and inert. SCOPE, restated because a sibling entry was originally filed with the wrong reading of it: SIFMA's page says verbatim that 'All SIFMA holiday recommendations apply to the trading of U.S. dollar-denominated government securities...', so its three regional panels are three TIME ZONES of one US-dollar market, not three asset classes — this is the LONDON SESSION OF THE US DOLLAR BOND MARKET, and UK gilts are out of scope. THE HEADLINE FINDING, and it is a downgrade of the proposal's own framing: this card is the corridor's SYNCHRONIZING day, not one of its desyncs. Measured on two central-bank primaries rather than asserted — the Bank of England's SONIA series (IUDSOIA, 7,498 observations 1997-01-02 to 2026-09-04, via FRED after the BoE endpoint's 302; SONIA publishes on every London banking business day) as the London session record, and the Federal Reserve's H.15 DGS10 (268,619 bytes, fetched direct) as the US bond session record. Across the 29 turns of the year 1997/98 through 2025/26, counting the Dec-24-to-Jan-5 window, New York's bond desk works AT LEAST as many days as London's in 29 of 29 (mean +1.17 sessions; gap distribution 1:25, 2:3, 3:1 — never 0, never negative). The 2026/27 window projects to the modal shape exactly: 6 London business days against 7 New York bond sessions, with EXACTLY ONE desync day — 2026-12-28, which this calendar already tracks as sifma-uk-bond-market-closure-2026-12-28. 2027-01-01 contributes NOTHING to the divergence; it is a day both desks are shut. ZERO INFORMATION CONTENT, MEASURED: across 2026 and 2027 the U.K. panel carries 29 full-close BUSINESS days, and ZERO of them are unexplained by either the U.S. panel (a US full close shuts the whole dollar market) or gov.uk England-and-Wales statute (London is dark whatever SIFMA recommends). The panel's only three cards that neither explains — Juneteenth Sat 2027-06-19, U.S. Independence Day Sun 2027-07-04, New Year's Day Sat 2028-01-01 — all fall on WEEKENDS. So a sifma-uk-* entry is a cross-reference, never news, and impact low is a measured verdict rather than an assumption. 2027-01-01 is doubly explained: the U.S. panel full-closes it AND gov.uk makes it statutory. THE PROPOSAL'S 12-of-12 TRI-MARKET CLAIM, EXTENDED AND CORRECTED: over both published years the U.S. panel carries 22 full-close dates and 20 of them are also full closes on BOTH the U.K. and Japan panels. The two exceptions are 2027-06-18 and 2027-07-05, where the U.K. panel lists the UNSHIFTED weekend dates (Sat 06-19, Sun 07-04) instead of the observed Friday/Monday the U.S. panel shifts to — a panel defect, not a market state, and the only two US full-close business days in two years with no U.K. card at all. PANEL ACCURACY, and this date sits in the verified half: the strings 'December 27, 2027' and 'December 28, 2027' appear ZERO times in the entire 299,272-byte page, against gov.uk's statutory England-and-Wales Christmas and Boxing Day substitutes on exactly those dates — the year-end defect the sifma-uk-bond-market-closure-2027-03-29 ledger located. The 2027-01-01 card is right. A TRAP DEFUSED FOR THE CO-DATED SIBLING, and it is this lane's genuinely new finding: Monday 2027-01-04 — the reopen, and the score-by date of three of new-years-day-market-closure-2027-01-01's forward tests — is a SCOTTISH statutory bank holiday (gov.uk's '2nd January' substitute, 2027-01-02 falling on a Saturday) that NO SIFMA panel lists. It does not shut London: SONIA printed on 24 of 24 Scotland-only statutory weekday bank holidays on gov.uk's record (2019-01-02 through 2026-08-03, including the one-off 2026-06-15 World Cup bank holiday), while printing on 0 of 65 England-and-Wales statutory weekday bank holidays — an exact detector in both directions, against a 96.85% unconditional weekday print rate. THE EVENT'S OWN CLASS: since 1997, 99 of 7,742 weekdays (1.28%) had NEITHER desk open; 21 of those are January 1 and 21 are December 25, together 42% of the class, and 21 of the 21 January-1 weekdays with data on both series were both-shut (the 22nd, 1997-01-01, predates the SONIA series by one day). IMPACT LOW and it stays low: symbols is empty, the date is estimate, date-keyed action requires confirmed, and docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md plus docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md were grepped this session for 'holiday|closure|london|sifma|gilt|sonia|new year|year-end|turn of the year' with ZERO hits in both. HONEST LIMITS: SONIA is a STERLING overnight rate, so it evidences the London banking CALENDAR, never USD bond volumes or spreads on that calendar; DGS10 is a close-of-business quote that cannot distinguish a 2:00 p.m. early close from a full session; and LSE's own calendar remains not machine-readable, so nothing here is asserted about LSE or gilt hours beyond the statutory gov.uk holiday. Kind rates, symbols empty and status estimate reuse the settled precedent both sibling U.K. entries follow.
